summary: Unexpected duplicate external actions when SDK retries function-calls after network timeouts
description: Customer reports that when their application calls the function-calling flow via the Redwood SDK and experiences a transient network timeout, the SDK's automatic retry path results in duplicate side-effectful operations on their downstream systems (payment webhook, order provisioning). They are requesting guidance on: (1) recommended client-side patterns (Python/TS/Go) to avoid duplicate side effects, (2) how to surface idempotency keys in function/tool calls, and (3) available server-side deduplication options we support.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer issues a function call via Redwood Python SDK that triggers an external POST (their webhook) from their tool implementation.
2) Network latency spike causes the SDK to hit a request timeout at ~s=3s and the SDK automatically retries the request (default retry policy).
3) Original request actually reached the tool endpoint but the SDK retry also reached the tool causing the external POST to be executed twice.
logs: Customer supplied client logs showing HTTP 504 / timeout from SDK then a subsequent successful 200 on retry. Server access logs show two near-identical POSTs to the customer's tool endpoint within 4s window. SDK trace: 'request_id=abc123, retry_count=1'. No idempotency key was present on the request metadata/headers.
investigation_notes: Initial triage by Support: confirmed request/response pattern matches SDK transparent retry semantics for network timeouts (SDK default auto-retry enabled).

SRE/Eng verified that the API gateway will retry on certain 5xx/timeout conditions and does not synthesize an idempotency key automatically for function/tool calls because function tool implementations are treated as user-provided endpoints with opaque side effects.
Reproduction in lab: reproduced behavior using local mock tool that logs side effects. When SDK retry_count > 0 and no idempotency header present, duplicate calls are delivered.
Risk: customer-facing side effects (billing/provisioning) can cause double charges or resource duplication if no dedupe implemented on customer tool side.
resolution: Action items and recommended patterns provided to the customer and implemented as a short-term mitigation in the SDK docs. Long-term engineering items tracked in INT-890. Recommendations: (A) For immediate mitigation—add an idempotency token header (X-Idempotency-Key) at the application layer and have the tool endpoint dedupe by that key with TTL; (B) Mark non-idempotent calls as 'no-retry' in the SDK call options when the call triggers irreversible side effects; (C) Server-side option—we added a guidance/feature request to allow Redwood to forward a generated idempotency token (opt-in) in a future SDK/console toggle so the runtime can help dedupe duplicate deliveries for function-calling flows. Customer accepted workaround: inject client-generated UUID per logical operation and handle dedupe on their webhook side.
recommended_client_patterns:
Python example (pseudocode):

headers = {
  'Authorization': 'Bearer <key>',
  'X-Idempotency-Key': str(uuid.uuid4())  # reuse for retries of the same logical op
}
resp = client.call_function('charge_customer', payload, headers=headers, timeout=8, max_retries=1)

Guidance: generate the idempotency key at the start of the logical flow and pass it through the SDK headers/metadata so the customer's tool can dedupe.

Go example:

id := uuid.New().String()
req := sdk.NewFunctionCall('notify-payment').WithHeader('X-Idempotency-Key', id).WithTimeout(8*time.Second)
// Optionally set client retry policy
req.SetRetryPolicy(sdk.RetryPolicy{MaxRetries:1, Backoff: sdk.ExponentialBackoff(200*time.Millisecond)})
resp, err := client.Call(ctx, req)

Guidance: use a single shared id per logical transaction and keep idempotency storage TTL on the tool side (e.g., 24h) to avoid unbounded growth.

Server-side recommendations: implement server-side dedupe keyed off X-Idempotency-Key and respond with 409/200 to indicate duplicate resource creation when detected. Log matched idempotency keys for auditing.
support_actions_taken: Added explicit doc snippet to customer ticket with patterns for Python/TS/Go and examples for embedding an X-Idempotency-Key in function calls.
Escalated feature request to product/eng to evaluate an opt-in runtime idempotency forwarder for function-calling flows (see related PR and INT-890).
Provided customer test checklist and small mock server code so they can validate dedupe behavior before rolling to prod.
Scheduled follow-up call with customer for 2026-03-16 to verify mitigation and answer implementation questions.
